vapt-report.use_alternative_when: Finding vulnerabilities at all: claude-security for depth, /cso for speed, and insecure-defaults:audit on its own for a configuration hardening pass outside a release.
vapt-report.use_bearing_when: A release needs a written, commit-pinned security position with threat-model links and a release decision.

webhooks.why: /cso Phase 6 only greps webhook routes for any signature verification and flags those without. webhooks builds both directions: raw-body HMAC with a constant-time compare, a 5 minute replay window, a unique (provider, event_id) row so duplicates ack without work, ack under 1 s, dual secrets during rotation, an outbound retry schedule with dead letter, a consumer-visible delivery log, and twelve TC-WH test cases.
webhooks.use_alternative_when: A quick security sweep for unsigned webhook endpoints across a repository.
webhooks.use_bearing_when: Building or hardening an inbound or outbound webhook integration.

workflow.why: workflow places the repository, branch, diff and gate result on one map spanning Bearing, Superpowers, gstack and GSD, and names the next skill whichever pack owns it. gsd-next is stronger mechanically, because it reads state through a script (gsd-tools smart-entry --json) and has hard invariants such as resuming a half-executed phase, but it only routes to GSD commands inside a .planning/ project. ui-craft start routes only within ui-craft and the gstack router only within gstack. workflow's detection is written steps with no script.
workflow.use_alternative_when: The work is already a GSD project with .planning/ state and the next step is a GSD phase command.
workflow.use_bearing_when: Someone asks what to do next or which skill to use in a company repository, across all packs.

autopilot.why: autopilot chains the Bearing stages from one statement to a prepared merge request, with every gate checked on disk by bin/brg-autopilot (a stage the model claims but the disk does not show is not done), every decision taken on the user's behalf written Proposed into one digest, and a hard stop before any push. gsd-autonomous runs planned GSD phases unattended and is stronger once a .planning/ roadmap exists, but it starts from a roadmap, not a statement, and has no decision digest or merge-request stop. Judged by reading; the end-to-end eval is the measurement.
autopilot.use_alternative_when: The work is already a GSD project with a roadmap and the phases only need executing.
autopilot.use_bearing_when: One requirement statement should become a reviewed merge request with nobody answering questions, and every decision taken must be reviewable afterwards.

docs-drift.why: gstack /document-release updates the docs a shipped diff touched, reading the diff. docs-drift answers a different question across the whole repository: which docs no longer match the code, whoever changed it and with whatever harness. Its script checks every path, make target and config name the docs mention and flags docs whose code moved on after them, prints counts, and fails on a broken reference or on zero docs; each finding goes to the side that is wrong, never a silent doc rewrite. Judged by reading; no eval has run.
docs-drift.use_alternative_when: A release just shipped and the docs it touched need the new behaviour.
docs-drift.use_bearing_when: Inheriting a codebase, before definition-of-done passes, or whenever a doc may have gone stale behind a manual or other-harness change.

verify-deploy.why: gstack /canary watches a deployed URL over a window for console errors, performance and page failures. verify-deploy is the ordered check right after a deploy, against the committed docs/environments.md: readiness, health, the deployed version matched to the tag or commit the engineer shipped, and smoke checks, GET only, with a report under docs/releases/ and a verdict; it never deploys or rolls back. Run it first, then /canary on prod. Judged by reading; no eval has run.
verify-deploy.use_alternative_when: Watching production for regressions over the minutes after a release.
verify-deploy.use_bearing_when: Proving the build you meant is the one serving, and that it is ready, right after a deploy to any environment.

speech.why: Read on 25 Sep 2026: Twilio's skills cover the phone leg of a voice agent (ConversationRelay message types, its interrupt event, streaming replies) on a Twilio account with Twilio's own speech engines. None covers engine choice by WER on the product's audio, diarisation, VAD and endpointing, a per-stage latency budget, or Indian and code-mixed languages, which speech measures with wer.py and latency_report.py. Measured 25 Sep 2026 against no skill (the Twilio skill is not installed): 0.96 against 0.88; the difference was reporting p95 latency against the budget and excluding broken turns.
speech.use_alternative_when: The calls go over Twilio: use it for the telephony leg and keep speech for measurement.
speech.use_bearing_when: Choosing and measuring a speech engine, building batch transcription or a real-time voice loop, setting the latency budget.

computer-vision.why: Read on 25 Sep 2026: huggingface-vision-trainer runs detector, classifier and SAM training on Hugging Face Jobs (paid plan) with mAP and accuracy; fiftyone-model-evaluation and fiftyone-dataset-curation do mAP, error browsing and curation inside FiftyOne. None covers few-shot anomaly detection, AUROC, a threshold chosen from the cost of a miss, group-safe splits, the VLM versus trained-model choice, or export and serving latency. Measured 25 Sep 2026 against no skill (the alternatives are not installed): 0.95 against 0.87; the difference was choosing the threshold on a held-out split and scoring test once.
computer-vision.use_alternative_when: Training on Hugging Face Jobs, or error analysis and curation in FiftyOne.
computer-vision.use_bearing_when: Choosing the approach, splitting by group, setting the operating threshold from costs, and shipping with latency measured.

tabular-ml.why: Searched the official marketplace and the huggingface, fiftyone and twilio skill repositories on 25 Sep 2026: nothing covers tabular or time-series ML (leakage-safe splits, a baseline gate, calibration, SHAP, drift). Platform plugins (sagemaker-ai, datarobot, databricks, dominodatalab) run jobs on their own platforms rather than teach the method. Measured 25 Sep 2026: 0.96 against 0.75 without a skill on two cases (leaky churn features with a rule baseline; seasonal alerting through a festival spike).
tabular-ml.use_alternative_when: The team already trains on one of those platforms: use its plugin for the job and keep tabular-ml's split and baseline gates.
tabular-ml.use_bearing_when: Any churn, scoring, forecasting or metric anomaly model.
